question.text: A risk-averse investor is choosing between two equity funds in the same SEBI category. Fund P has a Sharpe Ratio of 1.2 and Sortino Ratio of 1.8, while Fund Q has a Sharpe Ratio of 1.1 and Sortino Ratio of 2.5. Which fund should be recommended to this investor and why?

answer.text: Fund P, because it has a higher Sharpe Ratio indicating better overall risk-adjusted performance
Fund Q, because its significantly higher Sortino Ratio indicates better downside risk management, which is more important for a risk-averse investor
Fund P, because the higher Sharpe Ratio always makes it the safer fund
Neither fund, because risk-averse investors should never invest in equity funds

explanation.text: The Logic: For a risk-averse investor, downside protection matters more than total volatility. The Sortino Ratio uses only downside deviation in its denominator, so a higher Sortino indicates better return per unit of bad volatility. Fund Q's Sortino of 2.5 is materially higher than Fund P's 1.8, even though Fund P has a slightly higher Sharpe (1.2 vs 1.1). Because the Sharpe Ratio penalises upside and downside volatility equally, Fund Q's relatively low Sharpe combined with a much higher Sortino implies that more of its volatility is on the upside — exactly the profile a risk-averse investor wants. The Trap: A higher Sharpe does not automatically mean "safer", because it does not separate good (upside) from bad (downside) volatility. Asserting that the higher-Sharpe fund is always safer ignores the role of Sortino in distinguishing the two. Telling a risk-averse investor to avoid equity entirely is also wrong — they need a suitable equity fund, not no equity at all. Note: The Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook covers the Sharpe Ratio, Treynor Ratio, alpha, the Information Ratio, and investor risk profile on the cited pages, but does not define the Sortino Ratio or its use with downside-deviation reasoning. The framing above reflects general performance-measurement practice rather than a direct workbook citation.
